message: The replay expectation assumes the placeholder replaces only the second argument to `console.log`, but the implementation change is in `renderDebugModel` and may affect how the entire debug value is encoded/decoded. Can you confirm that replay still preserves the original argument count and ordering for multi-arg console calls, especially if one argument is omitted while others are retained? If not, this test could pass while masking a client-side formatting regression.

`field` events are now queued onto the current `tail` file whenever any file is in flight. If payload order is `file A -> file B -> field for A`, that field will be attached to B instead of A, so the decoded FormData can still come out of order or lose the original grouping when multiple files are buffered concurrently. Consider tracking the file that was current when the field arrived, rather than always using the latest tail.

`bodyFinished` is only set from Busboy's `finish` event. If a file stream emits `error` or `busboyStream.destroy(error)` aborts parsing before `finish`, `close(response)` is never called from this path and the reply promise can hang unless the error path closes it elsewhere. Please verify the error handler always resolves or rejects the pending reply.

`busboyStream.on('finish')` assumes every file has already fired `'end'`, but if a file stream is paused/backpressured or an error path delays completion, `flush()` can return early and this reports a global error instead of closing cleanly. Could this close be deferred until all pending files are drained rather than treating the invariant as fatal?

Fields are queued only while `tail !== null`, but once the head file completes and `flush()` advances, a text field arriving before the next file's `'file'` event will resolve immediately even though a later file may already be part of the same multipart ordering. That can reintroduce the ordering bug this patch is trying to fix. Consider tracking whether any pending file is still unflushed rather than just whether `tail` exists.

These tests validate the no-drop behavior for a very specific interleaving, but do not cover the case where a text field arrives after one file completes and before the next file event begins. Was that timing considered when changing from a global queue to per-file queues?

`finish` now relies on every pending file eventually calling `end`, but if a file stream emits an error after `finish` has been observed, `closed` stays false and the code reports a synthetic 'incomplete file part' error in addition to the underlying stream error. Could this double-report or mask the real failure path? Consider guarding `finish` handling after any busboy/file error or centralizing terminal-state handling.

Queued text fields are only flushed when the head file completes. If busboy ever emits a `field` after a later file has already completed but before the earlier head file ends, that field is attached to the tail file and delayed until the head finishes. That preserves payload order, but it also means a failure in the head file can now drop unrelated later fields that were already fully parsed. Please verify this is intended; otherwise fields may be lost on partial file failures.

`ServerReferenceId` was changed from an opaque type to a plain string type. Was this intentional for this fork? Making it a regular `string` removes the nominal distinction that prevents accidentally passing arbitrary strings where a server reference ID is expected, which can hide bugs in the Flight client/server protocol. If the runtime truly only ever treats it as a string, consider keeping an opaque wrapper on the public boundary and only unwrapping internally.

This entry point now only exports `unstable_prerenderToNodeStream`, dropping the previously public `prerender` and `prerenderToNodeStream` symbols. Any existing Node consumers importing those names will start failing at runtime with `undefined` exports. If the API is meant to stay backward compatible, re-export the old names as aliases or keep the previous exports in addition to the unstable one.

`ServerReferenceId` changed from an opaque type to a plain `string`. That removes Flow's nominal boundary and makes it easier to accidentally pass arbitrary strings where a server reference ID is expected. Was the opacity intentionally dropped for this fork, or should this stay opaque to preserve type-safety across the client/server boundary?

`processed_keys.add(get_validation_alias(field))` is now applied for every parameter type handled by `request_params_to_args`, not just headers. If this helper is reused for query/cookie params, or if a field’s validation alias differs from the received key shape, this can incorrectly suppress 'extra' detection for unrelated inputs. Consider restricting this extra processed-key entry to header parameters only, or gating it on `convert_underscores` being active.

`translations.md` is now treated as one of the core docs. If this file does not exist under `docs/` (or is generated later than the other docs), `scripts/docs.py` may fail or start reporting a missing-docs error. Could you confirm the file is present and intended to be part of the required set?

`is_non_translated_path()` now checks `path.as_posix().startswith(section)`, but `non_translated_sections` contains `reference{os.sep}`. On POSIX this yields `reference/`, which is fine, but on Windows `as_posix()` always uses `/` while `section` may contain `\`, so untranslated reference pages will be treated as translatable. Consider normalizing both sides to POSIX-style separators before comparing.

The new untranslated-page check only skips files under `reference/` and a few specific markdown files. The old hook also preserved other non-translated assets via MkDocs' file resolution. Because the staging step now copies the English tree and only overlays translated markdown, any untranslated non-markdown assets under language-specific docs will silently fall back to English without the previous explicit handling. If that is intentional, fine; otherwise it may break localized asset paths.

`live()` no longer accepts a language argument and always serves `en/docs`. This changes the behavior from previewing translated docs to English-only preview, which makes it impossible to verify non-English output locally via the documented command. If translated preview is still needed, consider keeping the `lang` parameter and pointing Zensical at the selected language stage.

`getProperties().getLettuce()` is dereferenced unconditionally here, but `RedisProperties#getLettuce()` is not proven non-null by the diff. If a user has no `spring.redis.lettuce.*` configuration, this will now throw a `NullPointerException` during bean creation. Please keep the null guard or ensure the property is initialized defensively.

`outputRoot.relativize(layerDirectory)` can produce an empty path component when `layerDirectory` is created under a temp dir on a filesystem with a different root representation, which would make `layerName` empty or unexpected. Since the test later uses this value as both the iterator result and the expected layer name, it may not actually validate the intended root-destination case reliably. Consider hardcoding a simple relative layer name (for example, `dependencies`) and keeping only `outputRoot` as the destination under test.

`RepositorySystemSupplier` may return a `RepositorySystem` implementation that does not expose `shutdown()`. If so, this call will fail at runtime or silently be ineffective depending on the API version. Could you confirm the supplier’s returned type and whether `shutdown()` is guaranteed here? If not, the safe pattern is to guard this call or avoid assuming lifecycle management on the `RepositorySystem` interface.

Creating a new `RepositorySystem` for every `resolveCoordinates` call may be expensive, since this code can run repeatedly while scanning annotations. If this method is called often, consider caching/reusing the resolver instance instead of constructing and tearing it down each time.

`determineEnabled()` now uses `StringUtils.hasText(this.bundle)` for the top-level SSL config, but the PR description says the same empty-string handling should also apply to `RabbitProperties.Stream.Ssl`. Could you confirm that the nested stream SSL path is updated as well, or is it intentionally handled elsewhere?

The wrapper replaces `agent.callback` with a function that always merges `userHttpsAgent.options` into the callback opts. If a future `HttpsProxyAgent` version changes the callback contract or relies on instance state captured by the original method, this monkey-patch could break tunneling behavior. Consider using the agent's documented extension points (or storing a custom callback when constructing the agent) instead of mutating the instance after creation.

Could you confirm whether `toJSON()` without arguments can ever return array-valued header entries at runtime? The new signature allows `Record<string, string | string[]>` when `asStrings` is omitted, but if the default behavior always serializes to strings this broader type may weaken consumers’ type safety unnecessarily.

Comparing `new URL(redirectOptions.href).origin` to `parsed.origin` is stricter than the existing same-origin checks in Axios/follow-redirects in some edge cases. Redirects that are effectively same-origin but arrive with an equivalent hostname form (for example `localhost` vs `127.0.0.1`, or other URL-normalization differences) will still drop credentials, which may reintroduce 401s for valid same-origin flows. If that is intentional, could you document it; otherwise consider reusing the same-origin logic already used elsewhere in the adapter.

`own('params')` / `own('paramsSerializer')` look like presence checks, not the actual config values. As written, `buildURL()` will no longer receive the caller-provided params or serializer, so normal query-string serialization appears broken. Please pass the property values guarded by the `own()` check instead of the check result itself.

Should inherited `socketPath` values be ignored only for security hardening, or is there any supported configuration path that still depends on prototype-derived values? This change intentionally blocks them, but it is a behavior change worth documenting for users relying on shared config objects or prototype-based defaults.

This early return bypasses the existing `value.length >= 1024` branch that decrements `counter.objectLimit`. Before this change, large strings consumed the debug object budget; now strings over 1,000,000 characters emit a placeholder without consuming that budget, so a payload with many huge strings can still produce an unbounded number of placeholder entries and defeat the limiter. Consider applying the object-limit check/decrement before returning the placeholder, or duplicating it inside this branch.

`yaml.unsafe_load()` will construct arbitrary Python objects from `docs/en/mkdocs.yml`. Because this script is likely run in local/CI workflows against repository content, a malicious change to the docs config could execute code during the docs build. Please use `yaml.safe_load()` or the prior MkDocs YAML loader unless there is a specific trusted-only reason to allow unsafe tags.

`RepositorySystemSupplier` is provided by the separate `org.apache.maven.resolver:maven-resolver-supplier` artifact, not by the resolver API/impl artifacts used by the previous code. I don't see a corresponding build dependency change in this PR, so this import will fail to compile unless the module already has that artifact on its compile classpath. Please add the supplier dependency or keep using the service locator setup.

This adds coverage only for `properties.getSsl()`. The PR description says the same empty-string handling is fixed for `RabbitProperties.Stream.Ssl`, but there is no corresponding production-code change or test in this diff. If `Stream.Ssl.determineEnabled()` still treats `bundle != null` as enabling SSL, `spring.rabbitmq.stream.ssl.bundle=` will continue to enable SSL unexpectedly. Please update the stream SSL logic and add a stream-specific regression test.

This cached tunneling agent now closes over the first `userHttpsAgent.options` via `originTLSOptions`. Because the agent is stored in `cache` and reused for matching proxy settings, later requests through the same proxy but with a different `httpsAgent` can still use the first request's TLS options for the origin. In the worst case, a request that used `rejectUnauthorized: false` can cause subsequent requests that expected normal verification to inherit that relaxed policy. Include the relevant `userHttpsAgent.options` in the cache key, avoid caching agents with per-request TLS options, or apply the TLS options from the current request rather than from the cached callback closure.

This restores `auth` whenever the next URL matches the original request origin, even if a previous hop in the redirect chain went cross-origin. For example, `original.example` -> `evil.example` -> `original.example/sensitive` would send the original Basic credentials on the final request, letting the cross-origin hop steer an authenticated request back to the original origin. To preserve the intended “same-origin redirects only” behavior, consider comparing the redirect target to the immediately preceding request origin (available via `requestDetails` in `dispatchBeforeRedirect`) or marking the chain as credential-ineligible once any cross-origin redirect occurs.

This change removes the previously exported `prerender` and `prerenderToNodeStream` symbols and only re-exports `unstable_prerenderToNodeStream`. In a 19.1.x patch release, dropping existing exports is a runtime breaking change for consumers importing the old names. If this was intended, consider keeping backward-compatible aliases (or guarded exports) for the old API names.

`processed_keys.add(get_validation_alias(field))` is applied unconditionally for all parameter sources, but the stated intent is specific to headers with `convert_underscores=True`. This may change extra-param handling for non-header params (or other alias configurations) by marking additional keys as processed and preventing them from being treated as extras. Should this be gated to header params (and only when underscore conversion is enabled) to avoid behavior changes outside headers?

`yaml.unsafe_load` is used to parse `mkdocs.yml`. Unsafe loader can construct arbitrary Python objects and is dangerous for config files that may come from branches/PRs or local untrusted edits. Please switch to `yaml.safe_load` (or a constrained loader) for config parsing.

This assumes `HttpsProxyAgent` exposes a callable instance property `callback`. In newer `https-proxy-agent`/`agent-base` variants the hook is `connect(...)` (or otherwise not exposed as `callback`), so `const callback = agent.callback` can be `undefined` and `callback.call(...)` will throw at runtime for proxied HTTPS requests. Consider feature-detecting the hook (`callback` vs `connect`) or applying TLS option merging via a supported extension point instead of patching a private/internal property.

`beforeRedirectAuth` depends entirely on `redirectOptions.href` being present (`new URL(redirectOptions.href)`). If `follow-redirects` ever invokes `beforeRedirect` with only component fields (`protocol`/`hostname`/`path`) or a relative target without `href`, this throws and is silently ignored, causing auth to be dropped even on same-origin redirects. Consider deriving the redirect URL from available option fields when `href` is missing, rather than fail-open to stripping in all such cases.

Truncating an arbitrary string with `slice(0, 1023)` can split a UTF-16 surrogate pair in half (e.g., an emoji or certain non-Latin characters) if it lands on the boundary. While modern V8 environments safely escape unpaired surrogates in `JSON.stringify` (producing sequences like `"\ud83d"`), this may still result in rendering a broken character block (like ) in DevTools. Consider checking if the character at index 1022 is a high surrogate before slicing, and decrementing the slice index by 1 if it is.

If `flush()` throws an error internally (e.g. from `resolveFileComplete` or `resolveField`), it consumes the error, calls `busboyStream.destroy(error)`, and returns out of the loop. If `flush()` was called by the `finish` event handler (or if the `finish` event handler happens to execute shortly after while the stream is destroying), `closed` remains false. This subsequently triggers `reportGlobalError(..., new Error('Reply finished with incomplete file part.'))`, polluting the response with a generic secondary error rather than surfacing the original parsing error that triggered `destroy()`. Consider verifying `!busboyStream.destroyed` or tracking initialization of destruction.
Since the local variable `lettuce` is already assigned on line 158, you can use `lettuce.getShutdownTimeout()` here instead of repeatedly calling `getProperties().getLettuce().getShutdownTimeout()`.

Including the `--launcher` flag causes the command to extract launcher classes directly into the destination folder. Because the destination is purposefully set to the file system root (`/` or `C:\`), the test will attempt to extract any non-application test files (e.g., `test/spring-boot-loader/...`) directly to the host's root directory (e.g., `/test/`). On UNIX environments running without root privileges, this results in an `AccessDeniedException` and causes the test to fail. On environments where writes to root are permitted, this results in system pollution. To fix this, remove `--launcher` from the `runCommand` arguments. The `--layers` flag is sufficient to verify the layer directory fix.

`MavenRepositorySystemUtils.newSession()` has been deprecated since Maven Resolver 1.9.0. It creates a `DefaultRepositorySystemSession` which skips modern resource cleanup. It is recommended to use `SessionBuilder` to create a `CloseableSession` and clean it up after use to prevent potential resource leaks.

The PR description states that this 'also fixes the same empty-string handling in RabbitProperties.Stream.Ssl', but the diff only modifies `RabbitProperties.Ssl`. It appears the corresponding update for `Stream.Ssl` (and its related test) was unintentionally omitted from this commit.

The PR description explicitly states this was swapped to an `AxiosError` throwing `ERR_BAD_OPTION_VALUE` and that the missing `AxiosError` import was added. However, the code here only adds `new` to a standard `TypeError`. The intended change was likely not staged.

The PR states this was changed to an `AxiosError` without an error code so that tests can correctly distinguish it from `ERR_FORM_DATA_DEPTH_EXCEEDED` errors. It still throws a bare `Error`, suggesting the modification is missing from this commit.

Similar to the other files, this still throws a standard `TypeError` instead of the `AxiosError` detailed in the pull request description. The subsequent boundary length check on line 80 also contains an unstaged `AxiosError` conversion.

This now truncates any string with length >= 1024 before `JSON.stringify`, which changes existing behavior for the already-supported “large string” path. In particular, a 1,000,001-character string that is already replaced by the server placeholder will now be further sliced to 1023 chars in performance-track descriptions, so the placeholder text no longer matches the full omitted-string message. If that mismatch is intentional, consider using a separate cap for placeholder strings so you don't lose the exact omission message.

The new omission threshold is `> 1000000`, while the surrounding comments and tests describe the cap as “longer than 1,000,000”. Can you confirm the boundary is intended to be strictly greater than 1,000,000 characters? If the goal is to omit exactly 1,000,000 and above, this should be `>= 1000000`.

`flush()` advances `head` as soon as the current file is marked complete, even if a later pending file has already been enqueued but has not yet emitted `end`. Because `busboy` can emit `finish` after the last file part has been fully parsed but before some earlier file streams have drained, this can close the response while a later file is still pending and drop its queued fields. Consider tracking a per-file 'ready to flush' condition or only closing once the entire pending list is complete.

`flush()` advances `head` as soon as the current file is marked complete, even if a later pending file has already been enqueued but has not yet emitted `end`. In multipart payloads with interleaved files, this can close the response before all file streams have finished and may still lose queued FormData entries. The completion check needs to account for any in-flight files still present in the list.

`encoding.toLowerCase()` assumes busboy always supplies a non-null string, but busboy's file metadata can be absent or differently shaped depending on parser/version. If `encoding` is ever `undefined`, this will throw and abort the reply unexpectedly. Guard the value before calling string methods.

The helper manually serializes multipart bodies and relies on `blob.name`/`blob.type` inspection. Is this test actually exercising the same browser `FormData` encoding path as production? If not, it may miss the busboy ordering behavior that motivated the fix. Using the native `FormData`/`encodeReply` path for both construction and parsing would better validate the regression.

The new `bodyFinished`/`closed` state assumes busboy's `'finish'` can only happen after all file `'end'` events. If that invariant is violated by an error path or a malformed upload, `flush()` returns early and the fallback `reportGlobalError()` is emitted, but the response is never explicitly closed/aborted here. That can leave the thenable unresolved or resource cleanup dependent on downstream error handling. It may be safer to call `reportGlobalError` and `close`/`destroy` the response explicitly on this path.

Same completion path as the other server variants: if a queued field causes `resolveField()` to throw after the last file ends, the code destroys the busboy stream but does not immediately transition the response to a terminal state. Since `finish` has already been observed or may never arrive after destroy, this can strand the request. Please verify that `busboyStream.destroy(error)` always leads to `reportGlobalError`/close on all supported busboy versions.

Adding `Exclude` as a readonly global can mask real undefined-variable errors in Flow/JS files. If this identifier is only needed for a specific generated file or environment, it would be safer to scope it to the relevant override instead of making it globally accepted.

This package now exports only `unstable_prerenderToNodeStream`, dropping the previously exported `prerender` and `prerenderToNodeStream` symbols. Any existing Node consumers importing those stable names will break at runtime. If this is meant to be a compatibility-preserving backport, consider re-exporting the old names as aliases to the unstable API.

`processed_keys.add(get_validation_alias(field))` marks the original alias as consumed even when it differs from `alias` for non-header parameters too. If this helper is shared by query/cookie/body extraction, that extra key may suppress legitimate extras or change duplicate handling outside the header case. Consider restricting this to header params or guarding it on `convert_underscores=True`.

This test asserts a 422 for an underscore header, but the request sends only the underscore form. If the intended behavior is to reject underscore headers only when a hyphenated alias exists, could you add a case covering both headers together to ensure the new processing logic doesn't accidentally drop a valid hyphenated value?

`_check_id_valid` now validates for NUL and then delegates to `_check_single_line`, which means a value containing both a NUL and a newline will raise the newline error instead of the existing NUL-specific error. If downstream code or tests depend on the prior error semantics, this is a behavior change worth calling out; consider preserving the NUL check as the final/only error for mixed-invalid inputs or documenting the new precedence.

`translation-banner.md` is treated like a normal translated page and then passed through `add_markdown_notice()`, which nests the banner inside itself for any translation that has a local `translation-banner.md`. This can duplicate the banner content or render it in the wrong place. If the intent is to override the banner text, write the banner file verbatim to the staged location and skip notice insertion for that file.

`config['extra_css']` and `config['extra_javascript']` are indexed unconditionally for non-English builds. If either key is absent in `docs/en/mkdocs.yml`, this will raise a `KeyError` and abort the build. Consider using `config.get(..., [])` or `setdefault` before rewriting these lists.

`copy_zensical_stage_to_site()` now always copies from `zensical_src_path / lang / 'site'`, but `build_zensical_lang_to_stage()` computes the build output directory from `config['site_dir']`. If Zensical ever honors a different `site_dir` value or the config is changed later, the copy step will look in the wrong place and fail. Reuse the computed path instead of hardcoding `'site'`.

`build_zensical_config()` passes only `config_path.name` to `zensical --config-file` while setting `cwd=config_path.parent`. This only works if Zensical resolves the config relative to the working directory; if it expects an absolute or full relative path from the repo root, the build will fail. Passing `str(config_path)` would be more robust.

This now dereferences `lettuce` unconditionally. If `RedisProperties#getLettuce()` can ever return null (for example, due to a custom binder or a future change), `applyProperties` will throw before any Redis configuration is created. Consider keeping the guard or using a local null check before reading nested settings.

Inside the null-free path, the code still calls `getProperties().getLettuce()` again instead of reusing the local `lettuce` variable. That reintroduces an extra property lookup and makes the method less robust if the getter is ever overridden to compute values. Reusing `lettuce` here would be safer and clearer.

`outputRoot` can be `null` on platforms or test setups without a root component, and `outputRoot.relativize(layerDirectory)` would then throw before the command is exercised. If this test is meant to cover only Unix-like roots, it may be worth guarding with an assumption or deriving the layer name without relying on `getRoot()`.

`isFileContainedInDirectory` now rejects paths equal to the output directory, which preserves the old behavior for files but also makes the intent depend on `startsWith` semantics. Is it expected that a resolved path like `/tmp/out/..` normalized to `/tmp` should be rejected even if it was originally under the destination? If so, a short comment might help future readers understand why equality is excluded explicitly.

Wrapping `agent.callback` assumes `HttpsProxyAgent` will continue to invoke it with the same `(req, opts)` contract and `this` binding. If a future version changes that internal API, the proxy tunnel could silently stop forwarding TLS options. Consider feature-detecting the expected shape or avoiding monkey-patching internals if the library exposes a supported hook.

The test trusts `tlsOptions.cert` as the CA material while the server certificate is self-signed. That works only because the leaf cert is self-signed and also acts as its own CA; if the fixture changes to a normal leaf cert signed by a separate CA, this test will start failing for the wrong reason. Using an explicit CA fixture would make the regression test more robust.

The proxy teardown closes sockets after destroying the `httpsAgent`, but the CONNECT tunnel sockets are also left in `upstreamSockets`. Is this guaranteed to avoid hanging listeners in all Node versions? If not, it may be worth destroying `clientSocket` and `upstream` symmetrically on both error and normal shutdown to reduce flakiness.

`toJSON(asStrings?: false)` returns `Record<string, string | string[]>`, which is broader than the previous `RawAxiosHeaders` and may still be too narrow for existing consumers if runtime can emit non-string header values in custom/header-extension scenarios. Can you confirm the implementation never returns numbers/booleans here? If it can, the new signature will be a breaking type regression for valid outputs.

`beforeRedirects.auth` now runs before `beforeRedirects.config`, but it computes same-origin using `redirectOptions.href` before any config hook mutations. If a user’s `beforeRedirect` adjusts the redirect URL or host-related fields, auth restoration could make the wrong decision. Consider running the auth hook after the config hook, or basing the origin check on the final redirected request values.

`buildURL` is now called with `own('params')` and `own('paramsSerializer')`, but `own` is a function that expects a key. Passing the function object itself means the query params are never read from `newConfig`, so requests with `params` will stop serializing correctly. This should likely be `own('params')` -> `own('params')` only if `own` is a higher-order getter, but here it needs to return the actual property value from `newConfig` (e.g. `own('params')` is incorrect as written; use `own('params')` only if the helper is invoked differently, otherwise `own('params')`/`own('paramsSerializer')` should be replaced with `own('params')`? More concretely, the helper probably needs to be `const own = (key) => utils.hasOwnProp(newConfig, key) ? newConfig[key] : undefined;` and then call `own('params')` / `own('paramsSerializer')` as values in the buildURL call, not pass the accessor itself).

`const transitional = own('transitional') || transitionalDefaults;` keeps a user-supplied empty object/falsey value from falling back, but more importantly it changes the scope of the later `transitional` read to this outer variable. If `config.transitional` is inherited or intentionally set to a non-plain object, the own-property hardening here may cause the adapter to ignore the caller's config in ways the previous code did not. Was the intent to require an own `transitional` object here?

The new cutoff is based on `value.length`, which counts UTF-16 code units rather than the size of the Flight/JSON payload the client has to parse. Strings at or below 1,000,000 code units can still serialize to multiple megabytes due to UTF-8 encoding or escaping, so they bypass this placeholder path while still hitting the expensive client parsing/replay path this change is trying to protect. Consider enforcing the limit on serialized/encoded size, or choosing a lower code-unit threshold that accounts for worst-case expansion.

When `flush()` is invoked from the `finish` handler and `resolveFileComplete` or a queued `resolveField` throws, `flush()` catches the error, calls `busboyStream.destroy(error)`, and returns without setting `closed`. The `finish` handler then immediately reports `Reply finished with incomplete file part.`, which can mask the original decode error until/if the stream `error` event is emitted. Track that `flush()` aborted due to an actual error, or have it return a status, and skip this fallback in that case. The same control-flow issue appears in the other server Node variants changed in this PR.

This public static Node entrypoint no longer exports the existing `prerender` and `prerenderToNodeStream` names, replacing them with only `unstable_prerenderToNodeStream`. Since this PR bumps from 19.1.5 to 19.1.7, consumers importing the previous names from `react-server-dom-unbundled/static.node` would break in a patch release. Please preserve the previous exports as aliases if they remain supported, or otherwise ensure this intentional breaking change is handled outside a patch release.

This unconditionally marks `get_validation_alias(field)` as processed, but the header lookup above uses the converted `alias` derived from `field.alias.replace('_', '-')` when `convert_underscores=True`. For a header model field whose `validation_alias` differs from that converted alias, a request header matching the validation alias is now skipped in the later `received_params` loop even though it was never added to `params_to_process`. That can break validation-alias headers or silently drop them for optional/extra-allowed models. The fix should mark the original field alias that the converted header name is meant to shadow, not the validation alias when it is distinct.

The staging overlay only iterates over `staged_docs_path.rglob("*.md")`, so translated non-Markdown files under `docs/<lang>/docs` are never copied into `site_zensical_src/<lang>/content`. Localized pages that reference localized images or other assets will either silently get the English asset copied earlier or produce broken links when the asset exists only in the translation. Copy/overlay the full translated docs tree, or separately stage non-Markdown translated assets in addition to injecting notices into Markdown files.

`RepositorySystemSupplier` is provided by the separate `org.apache.maven.resolver:maven-resolver-supplier` artifact. This diff replaces the manually wired resolver services with that class but does not add the new artifact to this module's build dependencies, so the module will fail to compile unless it was already present on the compile classpath. Please add the supplier dependency or otherwise ensure it is available here.

Spreading `opts` after `originTLSOptions` means any same-named TLS option already present in the HttpsProxyAgent callback options overrides the user's `httpsAgent.options`. For example, callback options commonly include a computed `servername`, so `new https.Agent({ servername: ... })` would still be ignored for the post-CONNECT TLS handshake even though it works with a normal `https.Agent`. Merge user TLS options with higher precedence for true TLS fields, while explicitly preserving CONNECT/routing fields such as the destination host and port from `opts`.

For same-origin redirects, this unconditionally assigns the original `auth` back onto `redirectOptions`. Because URL origins ignore userinfo, a redirect such as `http://other:creds@same-host/path` still passes the origin check, and any credentials derived from the redirect URL are overwritten with the original request credentials. Preserve explicit userinfo on the redirect target, or only restore when the redirected URL has no username/password / no existing auth to use.

`socketPath` is only validated when its value is truthy. With the new `const socketPath = own('socketPath')`, an explicitly supplied own value such as `false`, `0`, or `''` skips both the `socketPath must be a string` check and the `allowedSocketPaths` check, then falls through to the hostname/TCP request path. That can turn an invalid or disallowed socket configuration into an unintended network request instead of failing closed. Gate this on option presence/nullishness rather than truthiness, and perform the type and allowlist checks for any supplied value.
